# BLO-33503 — pod failures labelled from their shape, not one substring

[BLO-33503](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-33503) ·
[#1797](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1797)

## Files

- `src/server/execute.ts`
- `src/server/execute.test.ts`
- `src/server/job-manifest.ts`

## What changed and why

Pod-wait failures now carry a `PodFailureKind` set at the throw site, and the
caller maps that kind to the label. Previously a single
`msg.includes("pod containers to start")` test chose between two labels, so an
init container that ran and exited non-zero matched neither branch's intent and
fell through to `Pod scheduling failed`. That sent diagnosis to node, quota and
affinity for a pod that had been placed and had already executed a container.
Unrecognised failures now read `Pod failure (unclassified)` rather than
inheriting the scheduling category — a default that declines to classify is
preferable to a confident wrong one.

`errorCode` deliberately stays `k8s_pod_schedule_failed` for every kind. At
least six server-side sites key on it to mean "cannot prove external work never
began", and that count is a **floor, not a closed list**: it was four when this
change was written and master grew two more
(`reclassifyK8sReplacementLaunchFailureAfterThrottle`, `metrics.ts`
`retainSourceIds`) while the PR was in review. The in-code comment names all six
and carries the grep that regenerates them, because that enumeration is the
artifact a future editor would audit before splitting the code — and writing it
as a closed list would terminate that search early.

### Native sidecars are not the cause of a pod failure

The init-failure loop runs before the `phase === "Failed"` branch and originally
treated any non-zero-terminated init container as the cause. With `enableDocker`,
`initContainers` is `[write-prompt, dind]`, and `dind` carries its own
`restartPolicy: "Always"` — a native sidecar, which overrides the pod-level
`Never` and terminates when the main container exits. A pod driven to
`phase=Failed` by an OOMKilled `claude` therefore carried a `dind` terminated
status collateral to that exit, and the loop threw on it first:
`Init container "dind" failed with exit code 137`, discarding
`describePodTerminatedError`'s `claude exited 137 (OOMKilled)`. That is the same
mislabel class this change removes, aimed at the docker toolchain instead of the
agent container.

Sidecars are skipped for their *terminated* state only. One stuck in
`ImagePullBackOff` or `CrashLoopBackOff` still blocks startup and is still named.

### Review follow-ups

- Dropped the `(c as { restartPolicy?: string })` cast in front of the sidecar
  detection, and the matching `V1Container & { restartPolicy?: string }`
  intersection plus its stale "the client type predates this addition" comment
  in `job-manifest.ts`. `@kubernetes/client-node` already declares
  `restartPolicy` on `V1Container`, so both were re-declaring a field the client
  has — and a re-declaration compiles against a client that no longer has it.
  Simulated an upstream rename: with the cast, `execute.ts` produced zero type
  errors and `sidecarNames` silently went empty, returning the DinD mislabel with
  no compile error and no test failure (both sidecar tests hand-build the pod
  object); without it, `tsc` fails in both files.
- Relabelled the `terminated` kind from `Pod terminated before startup` to
  `Pod terminated before log streaming`. `describePodTerminatedError` emits
  `claude exited 137 (OOMKilled)` only when the main container has a terminated
  state, so the old label contradicted the evidence printed beside it.
  `waitForPod` returns when logs can be streamed, and that is the boundary the
  label names.
- Noted at the `PodFailureKind` union that `image_pull` and `crash_loop` are
  main-container-only — the init loop records both as `init_container` — so the
  six labels do not partition the ten throw sites 1:1.

The cast-free sidecar detection's comment originally justified itself against "a
rename **or a downgrade inside the declared `^1.0.0` range**". The downgrade half
is unreachable: `@kubernetes/client-node` declares `'restartPolicy'?: string` on
`V1Container` at 1.0.0 (`V1Container.d.ts:69`) as well as at the resolved 1.4.0
(`:70`), so no version in the declared range drops the field — verified by
unpacking the 1.0.0 tarball rather than reading the resolved tree. The downgrade
clause was dropped and the rename argument kept, that one having been reproduced.

## Why this entry is a file and not a row

The four rows this consolidates were appended to
[PROVENANCE-CHANGES.md](../PROVENANCE-CHANGES.md) before that file was frozen.
They are the reason this PR was ejected from the merge queue for `merge_conflict`
on 2026-10-03 — the exact loop `PROVENANCE-CHANGES.d/` exists to end.

Worth recording, because it is invisible to every local check: rebasing this
branch onto master produced **no conflict stop at all**, and the resulting file
held five BLO-33503 rows where the branch head had four. `merge=union` turned an
in-branch *edit* into an *add* and resurrected the pre-correction version of the
first row — the superseded "closed list" claim sitting directly above the
correction that calls it a floor. A local `git merge-tree` reports this branch
clean against the very master commit GitHub rejects it on, so the union attribute
does not merely fail to prevent the conflict: it also hides the damage it causes.
